Thank you for contacting the D-Link Tech Support Team!
Problem Description:
Will this work with my 713p?
Agent Response:
The DWL-800AP+ will repeat the wireless signal of:
AirPlus
----------------------

Sony ZX Series Wired On-Ear Headphones with Mic, White MDR-ZX110AP These are great headphones for music and movies for the price. I have never owned a big-money pair of headphones & after buying cheap ones that I had to replace multiple times due to breakage, I decided to get these after a recommendation from a friend. After buying them for myself, I also bought them for each of my kids. They're great for average use... i've never been bothered by outside noise, they are comfortable, and the sound is of good quality. They also are much sturdier than the cheapie $10-$20 ones I've gotten before. (My kids haven't broken them, which is a minor miracle)

I do recommend getting a bag or carrying case for them (I use a Crown Royal bag:) it certainly helps protect them and they do seem vulnerable at the hinges where they collapse for storage.

The only thing my kid complains about is the wire is kind of short. I prefer it because the wire is nice and thick and never gets tangled. with my previous cheap ones, it was always the wires that were delicate & one or both ears would go out. These are so much sturdier. (I think he just finds them too short when he wants to sit in the recliner with his iPad on the table & watch his Minecraft. If you don't require your headphones to meet these specific and ridiculous needs, the length should be fine.)
text_fidelity_b: Sony ZX Series Wired On-Ear Headphones with Mic, White MDR-ZX110AP

But, with the better speeds now available with Cox, it was time to move to a DOCSIS 3.1 modem.

Installation was simple with the only struggle being getting the modem registered with Cox. That's a process that I can't do on my own in my service area -- I have to call in to Cox and provide them with the model number, serial number and MAC address info. Once they managed to record it correctly, it was a simple process to swap out the old modem for the new.

I like the new design of the indicator lights. It's still bright, but not the shining beacon in the night style of older Arris modems. The heat while operating is not bad, but it's still sufficiently warm that it's best to keep the modem in the open to allow for good air circulation.

So far so good. I'll update the review down the road should reliability be an issue. At present, a 5 star product.

NETGEAR 16-Port Gigabit Ethernet Unmanaged Switch (GS116NA) - Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I own 2 of these 16 port switches housed in a wiring cabinet in a closet and another, a [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Switch (GS108)]] at my computer desk mounted to the wall, and an, [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch (GS108)]] behind the LR TV, then another 3 separate bedroom TV's (kids and my br) have [[ASIN:B002NVOLGI Netgear GS605 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch]] behind them for all the various game systems, video devices etc. I purchased them to upgrade my network from older legacy 10/100 switches a few years back. I have always trusted NETGEAR, mainly because it was used by an old employer of mine. I am very easily able to maintain, GB transfer levels, and all devices on my network are able to pull great speed tests.

I used the switches to segment my network into logical groups, the cabinet, holds the main switch's that run to things like the modem, router, alarm panel, other WiFi AP's, and they connect to my other switches.

One pro tip if you have young kids in the home, make sure and keep the network switches where they (young kids) cannot plug cords into it. At the time my 4 or 5 year old decided he would help dad by plugging the loose end of a cat5 cable into a spare port on the switch. You can guess it wreaked havoc on my system causing crashes etc.

These have held up well to years of use and show no signs of letting me down. I will certainly buy NETGEAR again.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Plus with built-in Hub 1st Generation – Black [please see update below original review]

I bought the original Echo when it was first available for pre-order and have loved it. No issues. The opposite is the case with Echo Plus.

Doesn't understand me half the time.
Intermittent success using the remote.
Tried multiple times setting up groups to play music simultaneously in different rooms using it with my 2 echo dots and original Echo. Echo Plus responds by doing nothing, or playing a random song or stations, and nothing on the other units in the group.

I really hate returning things, but unless there are fixes in updates between now and the end of the return period, that's what I'll be doing. Seriously disappointed. Oh, and I called Amazon "help" so-called, and I knew more about how it works than the person I wasted 15 minutes on the phone with. It was a surreal convo.
= = =
UPDATE: This morning I got a call from Anthony, from Amazon customer service. First, I was blown away that they would call me to address my issues with Echo Plus. Second, he was knowledgeable, and in no hurry. While it remains to be seen whether every issue with EP is fixed, the problem with Groups was.

It turns out that Alexa didn't like the name I gave my group, it was that simple. My original Echo is black, my EP is white, so I called the group "Black And White". Suggestion: When setting up your groups, go with one of the suggested generic names--bedroom, living room, etc. Echo calls them "Common Names". I called mine "Backyard", even though my backyard isn't involved.

Regarding Alexa often not understanding me on the EP, Anthony suggested that I try switching from British english to American english. I'm going to try that, although I have used British english on my original Echo with no issues.

So, I've upgraded my review to 4 stars, and when and if all issues are resolved I'll be coming back to make it 5. Amazon support definitely gets 5 stars. Even though my first call was a disaster, the way they followed up was remarkable, and that's the important thing. Seriously impressed. Thank you, Anthony!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Plus with built-in Hub 1st Generation – Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW), I own ALL of the kensington line of trackballs (clearly a trackball nut). From the original Expert Mouse (using a serial connection) all the way to this one. I can see how some purists are very touchy about their trackball performing and as it becomes an extension of interfacing with the computer, it's critical that it performs well.

PROS:
* Nice compact footprint; Not too demanding for space.
* Comes with the little ergonomic squishy thingy for a wrist-rest.
* The ball 'stays in' the unit even if you turn it over! This is a new concept for their trackballs! (you can pop it out if you need to condense for travel)
* Scroll wheel is nice; A feature present only in the higher-end trackballs.

CONS:
* BUTTONS! YUK! The button has some kind of contact issue where if you press it gently enough, you hear and feel a little 'click' but you didn't actuate the button! You must press it harder, and get a louder firmer CLICK! (really kinda mushy) to click it! I have tried different spots on the button and it's all the same! This is ALMOST a deal killer for me, but I'm going to give it some time, see if the button wears in and that false-click goes away over time.
* Scroll wheel is not free-flowing like on the modern expert mouse. With that sucker, you can fling the wheel and it will roll atleast for a half-second or so! This one really resists movement so it's more like a mouse-wheel than a scroll-wheel. It does not have a 'ribbed' feel, it rolls smoothly but it's not a 'on rails' as other models.

My personal favorite is still the modern expert mouse. It's massive (like a little tank on your desktop!) but you can navigate quickly with it, and use it in the manner a trackball was designed to be used.

Hope my review helps you!
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW),

text_fidelity_a:
Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model I thought long and hard about a tablet, knowing that for me it would basically be a toy. Plus I already had a Nook Color. When the iPad2 reduced in price, I thought about getting one of those, but decided against it for the following reasons: (1) no Flash--and yes, I know HTML5 is going to make that obsolete, but in the meantime many websites have a lot of money invested in Flash animation and even restaurants use the silly format to show you their menus (geez, just give us a LIST already--I don't need pretty pictures to find out if you serve something I can eat) and (2) I'm already invested in the Android market and would have to buy many iPad apps that I already have free from Android.

I have not even used it for a week yet, but this a preliminary review with some information I saw requested in other reviews (not necessarily here at Amazon).

UPS delivered this a little before 6:30 p.m. I immediately plugged it into the charger and left it alone. It was charged by 10 p.m. (it might have been earlier, but the unit was away from me and I heard no bleep or flash that might have have indicated the charge was finished). So it does not take six or eight or ten hours to charge as I have seen claimed on other sites. By midnight I was attached to wireless, had gotten into all my accounts and Android apps and was happily surfing and rearranging my home screen.

I used this over the weekend at a science fiction convention. I did not use it constantly, but turned the screen on and off all day for about a 12-hour period, reading Facebook and blogs, checking the news and weather, looking at the convention schedule online, playing short You Tube videos, etc. Nothing excessive, but sometimes did have it on for a half hour to 45-minutes at the time. I also do not have a lot of widgets going, like the Accu-Weather and news widgets that come pre-loaded on the home screen. (They delete easily.) In that 12-hour period it never got below 78% on the battery. It's very quick and fast and responds to a Targus stylus (rubber tipped) wonderfully, much better than my Nook color. The resolution of the screen is impressive. Maybe it's not the new iPad's "retinal display," but it's very, very sharp and bright, even though I keep my brightness turned down to save power. I downloaded the Nook app and the magazines I subscribe to look gorgeous and are simple to read; if not, a tap of the screen makes the text bigger. The unit also comes with Zinio preloaded, an app I plan to use to subscribe to non-US magazines. Kindle books look nice as well, but to me this is too large for marathon reading sessions. I prefer my Nook Color for that. Like my Android phone and my Nook Color, it connects to wireless like a dream, which is more than I can say for my laptop.

Things that might lead you to choose another tablet: (1) The camera is nothing special. It takes good close ups, but further away was problematic. However, I was in a low-light situation each time. Taking photos outside may be totally different. Why Samsung chose to remove the flash I have no idea. Silly, really. But who buys a tablet to take pictures with? (2) With a stylus I can tap to enlarge an image (like Google Maps), but not make it smaller and there is no plus or minus sign on the screen as on my Android phone. (3) Blogger doesn't work in the browser; you have to download the Blogger app, but that works well. iExit doesn't work on it, either. Rats. (4) As at least one other person mentioned, the screen cap button is right in a place where you can hit it easily. I thought of a good use for it this weekend (took a screen cap of the online schedule for the convention I was at, made a short-cut of it to the screen, then pulled up the screen cap for reference rather than going to the web page all the time). Very convenient! (5) Hate the pre-loaded websites in the browser, but I have seen this on other tablets. Apparently we the public are stupid (or lazy) and can't find our own favorite websites and bookmark them. [eyes roll], and (6) my Bluetooth keyboard won't work with it right now because there is as yet no driver for Android 4.0 (Ice Cream Sandwich).

I hope to check back with further comments.

[A few weeks later after I bought this, my husband found an Asus Transformer (TF300) at a good price. It appears to be just as good as this Samsung and the camera is better. It has a zoom and does take a better photo. So if you were looking for a tablet with a better camera the Asus Transformer may be for you. Note: It doesn't have a flash either.]

[Update July 31, 2012 to answer "How long does the battery last"?: I was sick and tired of not seeing any Olympic equestrian coverage except for a couple of hours in the wee hours of the morning, so downloaded the "Live Extra" Olympics app from the Android Market. This carries live streaming of events as well as archived events. This morning I watched about two hours of live streaming of the jumping finals. When that ended I watched six hours of cross-country eventing replay. Then about an hour and forty minutes of the replay of the jumping. I had my brightness at about 35%. This got me down to 10% of the battery from a full charge. Quite satisfactory.]
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655) We are very satisfied with the two DIR-655s that we have (at two sites). They hold up well and cause no problems. They're fast and stable; they run cool and basically require little or no attention.

Two router features that deserve much more discussion than they usually get are the unit's firewall (if any) and its Quality-of-Service (QoS) engine (if any).

o The firewall keeps external probes and hack-attempts out of your network. You'd be amazed how many probes a home or business broadband connection gets every hour from places like China, Eastern Europe and the Middle East. They're looking for ways in so they can infect your machines and steal your information. A router with a good firewall implemented in its firmware is increasingly essential. Firewalls let internal users establish connections with remote machines, not the other way around. And the DIR-655's firewall is excellent, a stateful-packet-inspection implementation that is truly industrial-class. Frankly, I didn't know this when I bought my first unit but was delighted to discover it once I brought it home. Good stuff. And, it's compatible with my company's virtual-private-network (VPN) approaches, which can be a real problem for firewalls to accommodate. My company has used two VPN approaches in the time I've had our DIR-655s, and there have been no issues.

o A good QoS engine prioritizes time-critical Internet traffic such as voice-over-Internet (VoIP). I did not fully appreciate this until we pulled the plug on our landline and implemented "roll-your-own VoIP", saving 90% off our monthly phone costs (see [...] for details). Only a router with good QoS capabilities will allow phone calls to be clear, crisp and smooth in the face of other Internet traffic. And the DIR-655 turns out to have a very good QoS engine. It automatically prioritizes the standard VoIP ports so our phone calls sound as good as a landline even with two teenagers streaming video, cruising Facebook, listening to Pandora, Skyping and FaceTime-ing, etc. Unfortunately, the marketplace is not yet fully aware of the benefits of a good QoS engine in routers, so it's not a given. Even Apple's well-regarded and excellent Time Capsule and Airport/Airport Extreme routers don't have it, for example. But DIR-655 does.

The only issue we've ever experienced with the DIR-655s in our years of usage was once when a cell phone got into a conniption loop that had it disassociate and reassociate with the router over and over and over again, many times per minute. This caused the router to bog down and reboot itself (and who could blame it). The DIR-655's informative logs helped me diagnose what was going on. Eventually the phone got straightened out, and the problem went away.

UPDATE: I can no longer recommend this router. The latest firmware is abysmal and ruins what was formerly a good product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655)

It worked BEAUTIFULLY for 5 months until one day out of nowhere, we, too, got the black screen of death that so many others have. It was still running, but the screen was black and my cursor had a spinning circle next to it. I am pretty good with computers so I tried all the usual fixes, and nothing worked. I’d always end up right back at the black screen.
BUT - I kept trying and I’m happy to report that I FIXED IT!!!

I opened a warranty claim with Lenovo & scheduled an appointment at Best Buy, but then after reading other reviews here, it was clear that this is a common problem. So I headed to YouTube. There’s a channel called PC Monkey & he has videos to walk you through all the troubleshooting for this problem. I tried all of the easy ones, but none worked. I ended up following his instructions for a fresh install of Windows from a USB - and lo and behold the laptop is like new again! It only took about 30 minutes to complete the process, and you will need another computer + a flash drive to download the install file.

I probably will not buy another Lenovo after this experience. I hope this review helps someone else who runs into the same problem.

text_fidelity_a:
Onkyo DXC390 6 Disc CD Changer,Black In a word, sound quality (OK, two words). If you have anything other than the most basic, low-end audio system, you will hear the difference in sound quality when listening to a CD on the Onkyo versus a DVD player. Highs are crisp, bass is solid without being muddy.

The unit itself is solid, and offers the ability to hold 6 CDs (and shuffle play). The changer works well -- no glitches so far after a few weeks of heavy use. Nice styling with an easy to see display. The buttons on the unit are a bit hard to see, but you'll quickly figure out what controls what.

The remote is not great, but decent. Good range so you can control disks from across the room. The buttons are rather small and don't provide much tactile feedback. I'm using this with an Onkyo receiver, so it can take advantage of the Onkyo interface (i.e., power up the CD player and the receiver automatically powers up as well and changes the input to CD). Only two cables to connect -- an optical out and the Onkyo interface cable.

The size is somewhat imposing (both height and depth). As other reviewers have mentioned, check the size specs before you buy to make sure it fits into the cabinet/rack you want to use.

Very happy with the performance, and find this to be an excellent value. Well worth the price!!
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo DXC390 6 Disc CD Changer,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) Let's begin with the cons:
This is NOT an Android tablet, even tho it looks like it. You CAN NOT download apps from the Google Play Store (at least, not without jumping through some hoops), the apps available on the Amazon Apps are sorely lacking in some areas (many of the apps I use and really like on Google Play are not available), the OS is slow and clumsy, the home screen is not particularly user friendly and the HOME button is only accessed through a screen, not a dedicated button, which makes it a pain in the butt (sometimes, not always.)
Now, for the pros:
Good size for a personal tablet, very durable screen and housing, and the biggest pro is the price! I got mine on sale for $39.99, and for that price, I honestly wasn't expecting a whole lot. I'm disappointed with the OS, but as a starter-level tablet, if you want to read books, surf the internet, check your email and engage in social networking, it's fine. I RECOMMEND it, even at the full price of $49.99, because for that price, you are NOT going to find any kind of name-brand table (BEWARE OF THE WEIRD, OFF-BRAND TABLETS! I'VE BOUGHT 3 FOR GRANDDAUGHTER'S USE WHEN THEY COME TO VISIT, AND NOT A SINGLE ONE LASTED MORE THAN A FEW MONTHS) for even a third of the price. Just don't expect the same experience you may be used to on your Android smartphone or tablets that you now have.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

NIXGIR UNL A1 True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones with ENC Microphone, HiFi Stereo Sound, 18H Playtime, IPX4 Waterproof Okay, so price to satisfaction ratio is one way to define the products' quality. It is really not expensive yet not so excellent either. So here is what I think.

Build Quality / Design: it's small and very conventional Bluetooth earbuds design, so looks very similar to Air Pods. Build quality is not so bad for its price and I have no complain about this part. The matt brushed finish does look pretty fancy but I don't know why they leaved some part unbrushed. So some part looks pretty nice but some look like just plastic. Yet, since it is $14, so I don't think I should complain so much.

Sound Quality : I am not so sure about this part. This does have all the functions which earbuds should have (touch control, voice calling etc) but it simply lacks the depth of the sound. It sounds like slightly improved version of Air plane bundle earphone, so not worth to discuss about base/mid/high range. For sound quality, something is off in the sound quality.

Ergonomics: So this one has old Air Pods design, you cannot change the soft rubber to adjust the size to fit your years. After few hours of use, I felt uncomfortableness and slight pain with this ear phone but I have small ear and I feel pain with Air Pods as well, so my opinion is not so important for this matter I guess.

Buy if you are looking for : some quick substitute for your Galaxy Buds / Air Pods / or other ear buds and price is very important for your purchase decision. Interestingly, this earbuds mic is weirdly good.

Don't if you are looking for : earbuds with excellent sound quality / very comfortable fit

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor I got the FitBit Versa because I wanted to try a smart watch without having to buy an expensive Apple Watch. The FitBit is comfortable to wear and looks nice. I like that it tracks my heart rate and steps. What I really wanted was to see my notifications on my watch. This watch allows you to see your notifications and will even vibrate to remind you of events on your phone calendar. It is lacking in a couple areas. One— you can see your notifications but you cannot interact with them at all. It also only shows text, so if someone texts you a gif or emoji it shows up as a blank message. It also doesn’t consistently give me my notifications, but that could be a phone setting issue. Second— the available apps are limited. You can play music, but only from a couple platforms. You cannot play Amazon music, audible, Scribd, podcaster... Also, the fertility tracking app for FitBit is ridiculously limiting. It is possibly the worst tracking I have ever seen. Since that is in the realm of health, I think it should be a lot better. It is effectively unusable.
So while this is a cheaper option than others and has heart rate tracking and such, there are still some limitations. It is waterproof— so I can wear it in the pool. Battery lasts about 3 days on one charge. And you can customize the watch face to your liking.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor

Echo Buds (1st Gen) – Wireless earbuds with immersive sound, active noise reduction, and Alexa I've been using these for a couple of months and find that while I like them, I prefer a competitor's product in terms of sound quality and the ability of the product to stay in my ear. I have tried the different options that come with them to get a better fit and stay in my ear tighter to no avail.

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. If they could make them in a way they stay in my ear, they would be perfect. Last night, one fell out and went into the garbage disposer. Luckily, it was not on and water wasn't running or it would have been gone.

As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

Overall, I do have a use for them. I love the ability to use Alexa. I wish they could do Alexa independent of a mobile device via wi-fi, which they cannot. I love the ability to recharge them from the case when traveling. The case is hard shell and very protective of the earbuds. The case is probably the best part of the product.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Buds (1st Gen) – Wireless earbuds with immersive sound, active noise reduction, and Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) [[VIDEOID:a23b5cd930e819bd2cae7872ede2dd37]] I decided to finally upgrade my Kindle from the first Paperwhite when I found out I could get a 25% discount and a $5 Amazon gift card for trading in my very old and unused Kindle Keyboard 1st gen, as well as other bonuses of 6 months free Kindle Unlimited (approx $60) plus a 30 day Audible trial.

I’m very happy with it and it has some great features.
I do like the adjustable amber tint, but I also really like the ability to invert the colors to white print on a black background. This is even easier on the eyes, but it does have a noticeable (and irritating) white flash every few page turns when using the buttons, and almost with every page turn when advancing with the touch screen. I believe this is the e-ink refreshing. I will probably use the black inverted color only when I’m reading outside in bright sunlight.

I also am really happy to have buttons to turn the page again. It’s the ultimate laziness to be able to just keep your thumb in the button and depress it to turn the page instead of having to actually move your thumb a half inch to touch the screen, but hey, why move a half inch when your can push down 1/16th of an inch? All that extra movement add up over the years.
The real reason I like the buttons is this: I live in Alaska and we have very long, cold nights. But even in the winter, we turn down the heat at night. I read in bed every single night, tucked all cozy and warm under my down comforter... except for having to have my hand out in order to touch the screen on my Paperwhite to turn the page. My hand starts to get very cold. It’s uncomfortable. My half frozen hand takes away from my happy bedtime reading experience. With the Oasis, I can keep my hand under the blankets and just push the button. You don’t know what a big deal this is until you spend night after night with a frozen hand.

I also like that you can select which button to the the page advance button and which is the page back button. The Oasis comes set up with the top button as the page advance and the bottom as the page back, but I switched them: the bottom is the advance, the top is the back. I hold my ereaders at the bottom sides, and had to stretch my thumb to advance the page when it was set for the top button. It’s just easier and more comfortable to use the bottom button. And this is cool: the bottom button stays as my page advance button even when I rotate the Oasis 180 to use left handed!! Smart!!

Others have covered the size and weight so I won’t go it I all that except to say it’s comfortable to hold. I do use the official Amazon Premium leather cover and it fits perfectly, and the magnetic closure/sleep/wake functions work perfectly also.

Dislike: Nothing with the ereader itself, but with however Amazon picks the “special offers”. From what I read, these offers are supposed to be tailored off of a person’s reading history/preferences. I may be wrong.
The books they are featuring for me are “romance” genre. I am sooo not a romance genre girl. I don’t believe I’ve ever purchased this genre in my life. I’m a hardcore sci-fi/dystopian. I have an adverse reaction when I see romance special offer.

Other than that, some of the complaints by others leaves me wondering.
I just don’t think it’s THAT big of deal that it has a micro usb. Really, it’s just not that hard to figure out the big end of the cable from the small end. As for charging speed, charge mine while I’m sleeping at night so it doesn’t matter if it takes 1 hour or 4. I suppose having to carry a micro usb cord and charger when other devices use a usb-c cord/charger may be annoying but I think I can find 2 square inches in my purse/pocket/bag/backpack for it.

Also remember that this is an e-reader. It’s not a tablet, computer or smartphone, nor does it make any claims to be. Expecting an ereader to function basically like a computer/tablet/smartphone is expecting too much. It does an outstanding job at doing it’s job as an ereader.

I have sent many different type of files to my Paperwhite using my kindle email address and it’s worked excellent with that old ereader, so I expect this new Oasis will do excellent with those as well.

My suggestion is to read the description fully and know what you are getting and what you aren’t.
If your reading experience will be destroyed because this doesn’t have (nor claim to have) a usb-c, then this isn’t the ereader for you.
If you want it to be like a tablet or smartphone or computer, this isn’t the ereader for you.

But if you love reading and buy this for what it’s made for, I can recommend it.
Definitely look into getting a discount by trading in any unused kindles, and take advantage of the free Kindle Unlimited and Audible while they are available to offset the cost even more.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

This soundbar can be easily wall mounted using the included template.

The entire system is intuitive and user friendly. While many sound systems require hours to hook up and figure out how to use correctly this one is so straightforward. The remote doesn’t have a bunch of excess buttons that you’ll never need or use.

In my instance my TV remote was able to control it immediately with no issues.

I highly recommend this soundbar for anyone looking for an easy way to improve the quality of the sound from your TV - and you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the rich sound it will deliver regardless of what you play through it.

I have a few gaming mic at home and I was just looking for something nice and programmable for the office. I thought this mouse would be perfect. For functionality it is. It feels great in the hand and the texture is perfect. Just 1 big problem. I'm a bit of a claw grip, and this mouse provides nothing on the right side to grab onto. When I try to lift the mouse to move it around (I like having a little lower sensitive at work as well) my figers slip down the right side. It's hard to describe but there's no lip on the right side like there is on other logitech mice (even their M100 mouse has more to hold onto) It looks like there's a lip on the right but it's really not deep at all and my fingers struggle to keep it from slipping when I'm picking up the mouse.

It's also slightly front heavy but I don't find that to be much of a problem. I've learned to live with it, I grip it a little harder when I lift, and I turn on mouse acceleration (because I'm not gaming with it) and everything else works so well it's hard for me not to use it even though there's this one glaring issue. Maybe you're luck will be different.

These are really small but they actually stayed in my ears and that’s also while I slept. They are also pretty comfortable. The battery life is awful. I have a few earbuds that last 3 times that and at half the price. Next would be the sound quality and that was also an epic fail. If the volume would have gone past the highest aloud the bass would have been a bit better. If you need to make or receive any calls, these will definitely not work. Every time I tried to use the phone features, the call would drop right after the hellos. The distance between these and my phone were was the only thing I found to be exceptional. What a shame. Yeah, the letters all wore off very quickly but I know where the keys are so no big deal. But it was finally time for a new one. The material on the palm rest was wearing out, etc.

I unpacked it and noticed it feels cheaper, oh well, not the first manufacture to make a product from cheaper materials as time goes on...

But the strangest thing... the little nubs you use to position your fingers are on the wrong keys??? On the left hand, it's under your index finger on the F key as expected. But on the right hand, it's under my middle finger on the K key. Makes no sense to have them be under different fingers. The middle finger, index finger I don't care but make it the same on both sides.

I already threw my old one out, and I could get it out of the trash but I tossed the dongle in the trash too would never be able to find it again...

The keys feel is Ok I'm not that fussy about key feel click, etc. but be warned that the communication on this keyboard with the dongle is terrible. It was bad on my original one and it's bad on this one. I was hoping there would be an improvement on that in the 9 years that I had the original.

In the end, unless there is something you really like about this keyboard (for me it was an ergo keyboard with no number pad) I would consider something else.

text_fidelity_a:
ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.
text_fidelity_b: ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included)

Sony MDRV6 Studio Monitor Headphones with CCAW Voice Coil I record interview audio for video/DSLR shoots professionally. My go-to system begins with a Sennheiser MKH416-T short shotgun mic into a Sound Devices 302 mixer (which can power the T-power mic), the line-in into a JuicedLink RM222 then into a Nikon D800, then recording to the HDMI output to an Atomos Ninja.

To monitor, I plug my trusty MDRV6's into the monitor out of the 302 mixer, which is listening via its return to the headphone output of the Nikon. With a knob turn, I can then listen to any of the mixer's three inputs directly or to the camera's return confidence feed.

If it sounds good in the Sony MDRV6's, it'll sound good in the edit.

Yes, there are way more expensive headphones, but I know how the MDRV6's sound, I trust them, and they never break.

The biggest problem is coworkers "borrowing" them and not returning them. Write your name on them in large letters.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRV6 Studio Monitor Headphones with CCAW Voice Coil

TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND) While there isn't as great a NEED for this as there used to be, as so many devices have built in wireless, when you have a tower that needs it, this is the answer.
Basically, because of even the higher demands (Skype, streaming, etc) you need that strong signal without drops, both ways. This has a feature called MIMO, which instead of the standard adapter that has one antenna for reception, THIS has multiple antennae to accommodate 2 ways, and to reduce drops in data.
Be sure you disable the anti-virus, failure to do so and it just doesn't work. If you periodically lose the signal and require a reboot, then uninstall the driver in utility, and install the driver only. Then use Windows embedded wireless utility to connect to your wireless network.

Go to the manufacturer site for some excellent recommendations, like if there's a reduction in signal after a few months, set the router to a static channel (like 1, 3, 6, or 9).
For the money, this seems to be a pretty good product, at least in my case.
I've had very good experiences this company's products, as well as customer service.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND)

Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished. Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.

That said, it does what it is supposed to do, it does it well and I am happy with it.

Setup is simple and easy. If you have your media ready to go, copy it to the included SD card and pop it in.

On a side note, the card that came with it is 32GB which is huge. That can hold literally thousands of full-resolution images from a digital camera. Assuming that the average high-resolution JPG image is 8mb (which is what comes off my mirrorless camera) it can hold about 4,000 pictures. That all said, this frame can also play back video and sound, so there is more to it than just showing pictures. In that light, the size of the card makes a lot of sense.

The frame is approximately 10” of viewing area. The images are bright and clear which should please most users.

The unit handles a number of audio, video and image formats. The list is not exhaustive, but it does handle the main types in each category.

Included is a little remote. The remote isn’t fancy but it is sufficient for changing settings, moving to the next media element, power on/off, etc.

There’s really only one negative, and that’s the documentation which is written in very poorly-translated English. I would lower my rating of the overall package on this basis except that the product is so self-explanatory and easy to use/understand that the documentation isn’t necessary.

Overall, we are happy with this frame. It works well and it is very easy and straightforward to understand. It handles a lot of formats and can play back audio and video in addition to showing still images.

Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. I used it in a Kodak flip-style camcorder/still picture taker and I liked the fact that I didn't have to worry about filling up the card.  I recorded at 720 and it did fine in the recording and in the downloading of the video--I really didn't notice any speed issues.  Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos. text_fidelity_a:
Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU Firstly, let me say that, being a closet tech-geek. I have owned countless hard drives over the last two decades. I own stock in Seagate, so I purchased [[ASIN:B000ND75C0 Seagate FreeAgent 500 GB 3.5-Inch USB 2.0 Hard Drive ST305004FDA1E1-RK]], (only the 1TB version) from them and, to my dismay, it just stopped responding to power after a couple of months (I got it working, but it was a let-down for sure with the stock thing and all). Then, I ordered this really, really expensive, crappy paperweight here: [[ASIN:B006Y5UV4A WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black]] (same basic drive, just an earlier model no longer offered, I think), and was ready to use it for skeet practice in no time. I hated that I needed to use their software to access the data on the drive. As for the actual software, it was a total PITA. But it didn't matter because, within weeks, the damned thing crashed for good--and I wasn't even doing anything weird with it. :|

So, about three years ago, I stumbled upon the Fantom Greendrive and was, at first, kind of put-off by the apparent size (it's actually not as big as the Seagate, it turns out). I really wanted something small and portable. But, after all those issues with other drives, I really, REALLY wanted something RELIABLE. I first did some research, took a chance and ordered this drive.

DEAR GOD. IT IS MARVELOUS.

That was, as I've said, three years ago. Three years of constant use: heavy data transfer, being knocked around (even dropped on the ground a couple of times), never defragged (I got lazy cos' it's so reliable), never disk-checked, numerous power-loss and disconnection incidents....nothing can kill it! It hums along nicely no matter what you throw its way.

You don't have to ever worry about unmounting it before you turn off the power--you just unplug it and go. It's never failed me and, to be honest, that makes it better than one particular husband, in my book (the second is doing quite nicely, thank you).

The "Green" is for:

---Firstly, it doesn't take a lot of power. Nice.

---Secondly, despite being dropped a few times, it hums nicely and quietly. No loud grinding at all. I always have to check to see if it's on (which is easy because a green light shines through the grate of the front to let you know the power is on).

---Thirdly, if you have it plugged in but haven't accessed it in a while (like fifteen minutes), it will initiate a semi-hibernation, then go into a bit of a deeper hibernation after like a half hour or so (never timed it, but it's cool when it does it). So if you hear a click and a sound like the motor is clicking off, that's what you're hearing. Cooler still, the minute you click to access the drive it's ready to go--little to no wait.

It's also very fast. As drives go, mine is almost full and THREE YEARS OLD and, like I said, never defragged, yet it still runs faster for data transfer than my brand new laptop...which makes me wonder about my laptop. ;/

I actually love this drive so much, I figured with my bad luck, one day it's finally going to give up on me and quit for good. So, about a year ago I purchased the newer 2TB drive[[ASIN:B002XITVCA Micronet Technology Fantom GreenDrive 2 TB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive GD2000EUS]]for more space and extra backup. I love having the two of them because, unlike many products, Fantom keeps the peripherals consistent, so the power supplies (though upgraded to a one-piece rather than two-piece on the newer model) are interchangeable, as are the USB cables (though the 2TB, being newer, is obviously a 3.0 rather than a 2.0). Still, transferring data between the two is easy-cheesy and fast.

So, all in all, I have to tell you that, despite being an incurable tech-geek, this drive is honestly the best, most reliable, and durable piece of electronics equipment I've EVER owned.
text_fidelity_b: Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9" I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9"

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator The good:

Lane guidance. I like to plan my turns and exits, especially in thick traffic. I hate it when the passenger who claims to know the way suddenly says "Left turn here!" to feet from the intersection when I'm in the right lane and the middle and left lanes are packed with traffic. No more. Tom Tom says things like, "Take a right on 17th street, then a left on Maritime Road, giving me time to get into that left lane." It also gives you lane guidance for exiting the highway, when it's right two lanes for this highway, and middle two for this bridge and left one for the other bridge. You can see on screen, and it tells you aloud, which land you want.

It tells you "left turn here", which is good when the street sign is missing or obscured.

It adapts quickly. It seems to know traffic laws, so it doesn't try to put you the wrong way on a one way the way Mapquest did in the early days.

It tracks your speed.

The route chosen to a familiar location surprised me, but thinking it over, it was the most direct route. I normal go one exit on the highway. It had me go a few very small side streets instead.

It works in or out of the car, for those who want to use it for camping or geocaching.

The bad:

Even on the loudest setting, it's a little hard to hear. The pronunciation is off, which one might expect, but the volume is poor. It's hard to hear, even with no one talking in the car. Good luck if you've got kids in the back seat.

It was a little hard to figure out. It wants the street then the number, and I tried offering the full address. Once I figured it out, it was pretty easy and did a great job.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019 This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019

After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)

Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.

text_fidelity_a:
MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White) Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.
text_fidelity_b: MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White)

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included. Most people purchase this wireless keyboard to use at home with their TV or other media setup. I actually purchased it to use at work as a more ergonomic option. No, this is not billed as an ergonomic keyboard, but the main issue I was having was reaching for the mouse, so I wanted something with a built-in trackpad. Surprisingly, there are VERY FEW options available, particularly within a reasonable price range (<50) and offered by a name brand company.

Prior to purchasing this keyboard, I tried another which featured the trackpad front and center ([[ASIN:B004KN7PZG Gear Head USB Smart Touch II Touchpad Keyboard]]). Unfortunately, that product was way too glitchy, and the size was not ideal. I thought that the center trackpad would work well given that I'm used to using one on my laptop at home (a [[ASIN:B00IPQXZ62 Dell XPS Convertible 2 in 1]], which has a near-ideal keyboard), but that did not seem to be the case. When I began looking for keyboards with a built-in trackpad on the side, this one by Microsoft seemed to be the only viable option, although I wasn't looking for wireless.

I did like that that the keyboard is Microsoft, and I like the clean look and design. Compared to the prior keyboard that I tried, this one definitely has a more comfortable feel. Although it is small, there is adequate spacing around the keys, something the prior keyboard lacked. There is no number pad--the trackpad replaces this--but as I never used this anyway, this is no loss for me. All of the keys are a nice size, including the shift keys (these are sometimes skimped upon). Unfortunately, there is no "End" key--I knew that upon purchasing, but I still miss it. What I did NOT realize is that in order to access the Function keys, you actually have to HOLD DOWN the "FN" button. This is a bit of a pain for me, as I use Refresh (F5) constantly, so this is now a 2-handed operation. This keyboard is also missing any kind of indicator for CAPS LOCK.

The trackpad is okay. I still have my mouse plugged in, and unfortunately, I find myself using it too often, as the trackpad is not completely reliable. It does accept multi-finger scrolling gestures, which is nice, and it does pretty well with simple up-down navigation; however, I have found that side-to-side is much more uneven. I do like that there is a left-hand click button on the right side of the keyboard, and I have made use of this at times. But I've also found that sometimes my palm randoming activates the trackpad when I am typing, causing the cursor to flip to a new spot on screen, which is annoying. So, at best, this has been just average.

This keyboard includes other features that I don't use--e.g., a volume control, a separate mute button (are both necessary?), home and other "hot" keys, etc. I'm assuming that these extras would be more beneficial to someone using the keyboard in a home media setting. For my needs, this keyboard has been okay. The layout is decent, although it could have been much, much better with a few minor changes. Depending on how you plan to use it, I would recommend it with reservations.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included.

ProtoArc Wireless Bluetooth Trackball Mouse, EM01 2.4G RGB Ergonomic Rechargeable Rollerball Mice, 3 Device Connection&Thumb Control, Compatible for PC, iPad, Mac, Windows-White Silver I switch between a Logitech M570 (thumb trackball) and a Logitech MX Master 3 (regular mouse) daily, so I couldn’t help but compare the ProtoArc Trackball to the devices I use daily. For me, it’s not a worthy replacement. It’s a backup mouse, or one to take traveling with me when I’m worried my favorite mice might get damaged or lost.

I do really like the adjustable angle of the mouse itself. The base allows you to set the mouse at 0 degrees or 20 degrees. That feature drew me to the trackball, and I think it’s implemented well. The mouse is rock steady at 0 or 20 degrees, but it’s easy to switch between the options. And because it’s built in, there are no extra parts to carry or worry about losing. For me, the 20 degree angle feels very natural, and that’s the one thing I miss when I go back to my usual mice.

The trackball itself feels sluggish and inconsistent. I’ve tried adjusting the DPI, but that’s not the problem. Sometimes the ball registers the movement of my thumb and sometimes it doesn’t. I did check the ball and sensors; they are clean. The ball is actually hard to pop out, I needed to stick a pen through the small hole to get it out.

The left and right click are soft and muted sounding. Which is okay, but then the scroll wheel click is loud in comparison. The scroll wheel has some resistance, it’s like scrolling through quicksand.

The mouse charges via USB-C.
text_fidelity_b: ProtoArc Wireless Bluetooth Trackball Mouse, EM01 2.4G RGB Ergonomic Rechargeable Rollerball Mice, 3 Device Connection&Thumb Control, Compatible for PC, iPad, Mac, Windows-White Silver
